subject: Banking
title: The Fed's Balance Sheet
description: Learn The Fed's Balance Sheet in one minute.

hook.text: The Fed's balance sheet reached $8.9 trillion in 2022. It holds more assets than the GDP of Germany and Japan combined.

buildup.text: Before 2008, the balance sheet was under $1 trillion. QE from the financial crisis and COVID inflated it to $9 trillion.

discovery.text: The Fed holds mostly US Treasury bonds and mortgage-backed securities. It's the largest holder of US government debt.

twist.text: Shrinking the balance sheet (quantitative tightening) risks destabilizing markets.

climax.text: $9 trillion is easy to accumulate and hard to reduce. The Fed's balance sheet may never return to pre-crisis levels.

punchline.text: From $1 trillion to $9 trillion. Easy to inflate. Impossible to fully unwind.

quiz.question: What is the Fed's balance sheet primarily composed of?
options: US Treasury bonds and mortgage-backed securities
